facts.raw_span: A Chinese woman in her late 20s presented with a 20-year history of progressive skin laxity
asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules confined to flexural areas
severe skin sagging occurred on her abdomen with loss of elasticity
no extracutaneous involvement
born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents
younger sister had developed the same skin symptoms
Thick and leathery skinfolds on the neck, axillae, inguinal regions, abdomen, and limbs, with yellowish papules scattered on the dorsal neck
Low clotting activity of factor X (52.2%; reference range, 77%-131%)
Prolonged prothrombin time (12.8 seconds; reference range, 10.4-12.6 seconds)
excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments scattered in the reticular dermis (von Kossa staining)
compound heterozygous sequence variation in GGCX gene
c.1167_1172delCTGGACinsGGGAA (p. Asn389Lys fs*13) in exon 8
A Chinese woman in her late 20s presented with a 20-year history of progressive skin laxity
asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules confined to flexural areas
severe skin sagging occurred on her abdomen with loss of elasticity
no extracutaneous involvement
born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents
younger sister had developed the same skin symptoms
Thick and leathery skinfolds on the neck, axillae, inguinal regions, abdomen, and limbs, with yellowish papules scattered on the dorsal neck
Low clotting activity of factor X (52.2%; reference range, 77%-131%)
Prolonged prothrombin time (12.8 seconds; reference range, 10.4-12.6 seconds)
excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments scattered in the reticular dermis (von Kossa staining)
compound heterozygous sequence variation in GGCX gene
c.1167_1172delCTGGACinsGGGAA (p. Asn389Lys fs*13) in exon 8

concepts.why: The patient's skin symptoms, including yellowish coalesced papules and thick, leathery skinfolds, along with the histopathological finding of excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments, are characteristic of pseudoxanthoma elasticum.
The patient's low clotting activity of factor X, prolonged prothrombin time, and compound heterozygous sequence variation in the GGCX gene are indicative of GGCX deficiency, a rare bleeding disorder.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of progressive skin laxity, asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules, and excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments are more closely aligned with Pseudoxanthoma elasticum, despite the genetic findings indicating GGCX deficiency, which is associated with bleeding disorders and does not fully explain the patient's skin symptoms.
